notes.title: Dev Update - 4/30/25
notes.content:
Hello everyone, hope you all are doing well.

[h1]v1.1.9.1 Progress[/h1]
Despite burnout, progress is being done. v1.1.9.1 is going to feature:
[list]
[*]some bug fixes
[*]Quality of Life improvements
[*]support for upcoming DLC (wink, blink)
[*]and improve the Steam Deck experience (on-screen keyboard will soon automatically appear when typing in input boxes and the game will [i]actually[/i] render the game in 1280x800 instead of it defaulting to 1280x720 for some reason.
[/list]
This update [i]should[/i] come out some time in May, but it's also going to be a very busy month for me between my birthday coming up and some academic events. Nevertheless, the update is coming out, and there will be more to come in the near future that won't be next year.

[h1]The Future[/h1]
As always; here's a reminder that [b]when v2.0 rolls out, the base price will go from USD$4.99 to USD$7.99[/b] due to a severe increase in content. Now that that's out of the way, I want to talk about some new projects.

[h1]New Games Coming Soon![/h1]
[i]I'm excited to (really early) announce these games I'm working on that will hopefully have a home on Steam when they're ready to release![/i]

[h2]My Amazing Life as a Shoe Disposer![/h2]
In this comedy horror, you'll be a typical citizen with the amazing career of being a disposer of used and old shoes (you eat them. yes. EAT. it's totally fine for your health.) It's amazing! In this game, you'll live though your amazing life and throw parties to share the awesomeness. 
In terms of development, prototyping has begun. There's a player-controller and a base house with a working door, but the groundwork for a basic alpha is there and shouldn't take long.

[h2]Primaldemic[/h2]
Primaldemic is an open-world realtime action RPG gacha game where the gacha is optional. You can also directly buy characters at any time. 
(They're discounted during their banner. 6-star characters are slightly OP, and can only be extremely rarely obtained from gacha.) Premium currency will use our standard pricing (cheap; USD$0.99 for 2 pulls worth, 10 pull is $3.99, and a guarunteed 5-star at 60 pulls would be about USD$14.99. About those pulls, your banner 5-star is always guarunteed once you hit 100 pulls. More details to be determined later.

In this game, you'll stop a plague that was caused by a rouge scientist as a bandage-cure for an unknown disease that wasn't nearly ready for the public. Side effects are turning ghoul-like and increased strength. Mutations may occur on severe overdosage.

In terms of development; it's in the planning phase. No prototype just yet, just a document for planned stuff and some soundtrack (yes I make songs for my games that don't even exist yet.) which you can listen to [url=https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Ews0rLzJ0WZbcUzO753sEKZqlzsLTuw8?usp=sharing]here.[/url]

[h2]MysticalDevelopers Legacy Remastered Collection[/h2]
A full redesign of my old Scratch games are going to be remade in Unity. This collection will include:
[list]
[*]Pellet Dodge: Classic: Remastered
[*]Pellet Shoot: Remastered
[*]Milk Drinking Simulator: Remastered
[/list]
Each game will have redone graphics and improved gameplay that expands but stays true to the original content. This may or may not be a paid bundle. Development not started at this time.


Thanks to everyone who's enjoying my games, and I hope you'll stick around to see what'll be new in store in the future!

notes.title: v1.1.9 is here!
notes.content:
Hey infinite copies of #274! This is a big change, as you can see below. I greatly improved the game in so many ways so I hope you all check it out, especially if you haven't played in a while!

[h1]-- Endless Mode 2.0! --[/h1]
- Leaderboards are back now using Steam
- Score now increases with enemy kills and score gained scales by how many enemies you kill in a Dash
- Optimized tracking of DashKills

[h1]-- Custom Level 1.5! --[/h1]
- The Custom Level setup screen is now simpler and better
- You can now save/load your custom levels as a preset in a physical file that you can share with others

[h2]-- Thanks ATOMFACTOR for suggesting and finding these --[/h2]
- Base Dash Cooldown has been reduced from 3 to 1 second
- Minimum Dash Cooldown (from upgrades) has been reduced from 1 to 0.2 seconds
- Coins now spawn every 3.5 to 6 seconds instead of every 10 to 14 seconds and now despawn after a flat 6 seconds instead of 10 to 15 seconds
- The Tutorial has been redesined
- Fixed the Main Menu not blocking back button input when opening a menu (this would softlock the game)
- Fixed an issue where the lava on the Lava Maze DashCourse didn't sit still
- Fixed ShipTrials not giving rewards

[h1]-- Other Changes --[/h1]
- The (mostly) full Settings Menu is now available in the Pause Menu
- Unity engine has been upgraded from 2022 to Unity 6
- Optimized Unity backend and rendering settings
- Fixed Settings Menu navigation bugs and graphical issues
- The parts of your ship that fly off in the Ship's Death FX now color match your ship
- Ship Color Customization has been optimized
- Fixed the ShipTrail not copying some Ship colors
- Added a spawn animation to the Player Ship
- Fixed Endless Mode powerups using the old Glow effect
- Fixed all non-glass materials in the Level Hub being made out of glass
- Fixed a bunch of other minor bugs and improved the Quality of Life of some situations.

notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
Hey #274!

  This is regular contact on what's going on since updates are slower than ever.

[h1]What's coming:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Endless Mode 2.0 - New score system and minibosses with Endless-exclusive rewards.
[*]Leaderboards will now use Steam (mobile and upcoming console versions will use something else, unless Valve one day adds cross-platform support for Steamworks services.)
[/list]

[h1]What's the hold-up??[/h1]
Short answer: Burnout. The worst enemy to all types of creators. I've just generally lost my motivation to do much in the Editor at the moment, since I've had to stare at pretty much the same stuff since 2021 (Wow, we're coming up to 4 years of total 'active' development!) so that takes a toll on how much you want to keep staring. The updates aren't difficult for me to do, they just honestly bore me. 

[h1]So, what about it?[/h1]
1) Rude. 2) I'm gonna try my quickest to leave Pellet Dodge off at a state that I can fully leave complete and be satisfied about it, while still having things I could possibly do to improve the game experience, or even do DLC. That'll be my end goal; to make a great v2.0.0. Then, after that, onto newer projects for the time being. So I can improve my skills and regain that excitement to learn something new about the project I'm working on. I've already got two 3D games in mind that I want to make that'll hopefully also be here on Steam. Please look forward to them, as I will be looking forward to developing them and experiencing your playthroughs when they're playable.

Leaderboards will now use Steam (mobile and upcoming console versions will use something else, unless Valve one day adds cross-platform support for Steamworks services.)

notes.title: Change of Plans!
notes.content:
[h1]Hiatus of Multiplayer[/h1]
Hey everyone! This is an occasional dev update to prevent radio silence, but I have a somewhat upsetting announcement. I unfortunately have to break my promise of v1.1.9 being The Multiplayer Update. Turns out, making a by-design singleplayer game multiplayer is extremely difficult, and requires a lot of time and effort that I can't put in without taking forever and end up not meeting a lot of self-made deadlines for updates. So, for now, multiplayer is pushed onto the back burner while I try to slowly rewrite some parts of the game to better support multiplayer. Current issues that I had with the first attempt were:
[olist]
[*]The input system was redesigned to only allow one type of input (keyboard or controller) at a time; with controller being auto-selected when controllers are enabled. The code is correct, but UI is still unusable with controllers, like it's not switching the input mode even though it knows there are controllers.
[*]The input system also doesn't automatically create new Players in gameplay, also like controllers aren't connected.
[*]To continue #2; All controllers will still end up only controlling the same main player ship when in gameplay.
[/olist]

I've done some debugging yet still couldn't yield results. So, instead of making update progress go to a halt while I tirelessly work to make multiplayer work, I'm going to put it fairly low on my priorities, while still working on it between updates so that [i]no[/i] progress is made.

[h1]The Endless Mode 2.0 Update[/h1]
So, instead of v1.1.9's main focus being the Multiplayer Update. I'm going to instead highlight it being the Endless Mode 2.0 update! This was going to be with the multiplayer update anyway, but this is now the main highlight of the update. The Endless Mode update will:
[list]
[*]Overhaul Score; making gameplay actually score-based and not just time-based.
[*]Add Minibosses to drop special buffs and grant a bunch of score.
[*]Add a lot more Endless Mode rewards and even an exclusive Endless Mode shop/upgrades (since technically some Ship stats are actually different in Endless Mode.)
[*]and some more things that I currently can't think of but will probably throw in when I do.
[/list]

So hang tight, I've still got [i]something[/i] cooking up.

[h1]Heads up about v2.0.0[/h1]
Sorry to leave some important information at the bottom, but before talking about v2.0.0, I want to inform all the people that don't yet own Pellet Dodge that [b]PD's price will increase to USD$7.99 when v2.0.0 releases.[/b] This is because v2.0.0 is going to be a huge content update that will increase the value of the game. It'll include the second part of the Base Game, first part Base Game story improvements, gameplay modifiers (to shake things up), replayability features (something sorta like New Game+,) and a lot more Ship customization options, as well as some other stuff I may come up with on the spot!
After v2.0.0, I'm going to take a hiatus from PD as a whole to start new projects and get better at making games. That doesn't exactly mean PD [i]won't[/i] get any new updates after v2.0.0, since there's still some stuff that needs to be improved [i]ahem, Custom Levels[/i] and Multiplayer WILL eventually be added.

[h1]I'm tired of typing now[/h1]
Anyways, thanks for reading this (sorry for the wall of text) and for playing PD! Your feedback is extremely valuable to me and I am very willing to look for any of it to improve the experience for everyone. In the meantime, keep saving the Universe, infinite clones of Ship #274; we've still got a lot to do.

notes.title: MysticalDeveloper's Unofficial Steam Deck Compatibility Info
notes.content:
Hello! Since PD is an unknown (gem?) game, Valve has yet to add information regarding compatibility of the Steam Deck. So, here's my own words to tell you:
[list]
[*]All content should work well using the default controller layout, as PD has had a long history of optimizations to controller support. (As long as I didn't bug anything.) 
[*]PD shows generic controller glyphs, but they still apply to the Deck's layout.
[*]The game runs a flawless 60FPS at the Deck's native resolution of 1280x800. The game also defaults to run in the Vulkan rendering engine on Deck for improved battery life.
[*]The UI is legible. PD has had mobile and small screens in mind since Day 1, so all the text is nice and large, but not too big. The font may be hard to read for some, but there is an option to change the font in PD's Accessibility Settings.
[/list]

tags.feature: The game also defaults to run in the Vulkan rendering engine on Deck for improved battery life.
The font may be hard to read for some, but there is an option to change the font in PD's Accessibility Settings.

notes.title: Soundtrack Permanent Price Drop & Important PD Announcement
notes.content:
[h1]The Soundtrack Price Cut[/h1]
Hello everyone. I recently published the soundtrack for all of you to pick up. The thing was it was at a price higher than even what the full game will be, which is worth the effort, but not for the cool guys that actually want to buy the stuff. So, I have cut back on the pricing and it is going to stay this price.

[h1]The Future for Pellet Dodge[/h1]
I want to thank everyone that has bought the game and enjoyed it, and I want to especially thank everyone who played it during its BETA phase and helping me over the past 2 years to shape the game into what it is today. The announcement I want to make is that [b]Pellet Dodge will go on a development hiatus when v2.0 rolls out.[/b] I'll still do minor fixes, but v2.0 will be the last major content update for a while. This is still a long ways to go, but I just want to work on new things to show off what I can do. Pellet Dodge is something I'm proud of, but I want to make better and more advanced things, especially focusing on 3D. I have two games in mind, one is an open-world 3D RPG in which is my personally improved version of a game I like, but lacks in some features (spoiler alert it starts with a g.)

Anyways, I want to now lay out a sort of expected roadmap of what I have planned. So, here's what I will try to work on as follows:

v1.7 - Local Multiplayer support (so you can finally play with your friends), Endless Mode score changes, Endless Mode Content Overhaul, and General cutscene and storytelling improvements (again).

v1.8 - Steam Networking support (Steam-specific leaderboards and more...), Endless Mode Tournaments (Steam-exclusive for now, as it will use Steam Lobbies), and Steam-networked Online Multiplayer (so you don't have to make your friends suffer by Remote Play latency when playing with you)

v1.9 - CyberCity expansions and basic storyline, as well as fixes and polish to make sure everything is tip-top.

v2.0 - The full first Stronghold, Completion of the CyberCity (DLC), Part 2 of the Base Game (I cannot assure this can be another 40 levels, I'm lacking in enemy ideas), and hopefully more things finished that I started.

Keep in mind that this order of operations is more of a suggestion and some things may be pushed back. These updates are also going to take a long time, depending on the amount of effort and my work efficiency.

Again, thank you everyone, and let's have some more fun in what's to come.

notes.title: Version 1.1.1 now out!
notes.content:
Thanks for checking out Pellet Dodge! After a long time of hard work, here's some of the things that's changed in this version:

- Save Files have been redone to now save in physical files, which now allows Steam Cloud to be supported.
- The Linux graphics API is now Vulkan by default to preserve battery life for the Steam Deck.
- The Steam Deck's keyboard [i]should[/i] now automatically appear when selecting an InputField.
- A lot of new and reaaaalllly old bugs have been finally fixed.

notes.title: Update 1.1.0 - Small Fixes... for now
notes.content:
Some big updates are yet to come, but for now is some small changes to improve the game experience.
[list]
[*] The UI and in-game camera has been improved for 4:3 displays
[*] Improved the pre-open-world areas of the CyberRyft to be one level
[*] Decreased the Area 10 Boss' difficulty
[*] The Pre-Release Main Menu theme has been added to the options of Menu music.
[/list]

Thanks for checking out Pellet Dodge, and we'll have more impressive updates later on.
